preview.note: Worth watching before a book study, not during one. It gives you the shape of the whole thing, so the book you are about to sit in has somewhere to sit. Write down the one thread you want to follow, and start there.

source.name: Harvous
source.attribution: Written for Bright Enough, the Harvous blog.

listings.title: Augustine's Confessions

listings.title: Bible Engagement Project — kids
listings.description: Kids' curriculum that follows the same scope and sequence as the adult and youth material.

source.attribution: Bible Engagement Project is the author and owner of this curriculum.
source.licence: The overview is open. The lessons need a free Bible Engagement Project account.

preview.note: Worth a look if your children's ministry and your adult classes are currently in unrelated places in the Bible on the same Sunday.

listings.title: Free courses

source.name: The Gospel Coalition
source.attribution: The Gospel Coalition is the author and owner of these courses.
source.licence: Free to watch. Some courses ask for a free account.

preview.note: Course-shaped rather than article-shaped, so it suits a term of preparation better than a single week. Worth knowing it is written from a Reformed evangelical position.

listings.title: The craft of preaching

preview.excerpt: Essays on the work itself — shaping a sermon, reading a room, and keeping going over years.

source.name: Working Preacher
source.attribution: Working Preacher is published by Luther Seminary.
source.licence: Free to read, and no account needed.

preview.note: Less about this week's text and more about how you do the job. Worth reading in a quiet week rather than a busy one.

source.attribution: OpenBible.info is the author of this index.
source.licence: Free, and the underlying data is Creative Commons licensed.

preview.note: A fast way to gather the passages before a topical study rather than working from the ones you already remember. Check what it gives you in context; an index cannot do that part.

listings.title: The Monday retention loop
listings.description: What to do on Monday so that Sunday's teaching is still doing something on Thursday.

source.name: Bible Engagement Project

preview.note: Useful when a whole church wants to be in the same place at the same time. The overview page is open to read; the lessons themselves are behind a free account.

source.licence: Free to read, and no account needed.

preview.note: Where to go on a Tuesday when the passage is not opening. Written for people who have to say something useful about it on Sunday, which is a different job from a study Bible's.

source.licence: Free to use, and no account needed.

preview.note: The one to reach for when a study turns on a single word and you want to see it in Greek or Hebrew without owning software. Keep it on the shelf; do not try to read it through.

source.name: Bible Engagement Project
source.attribution: Bible Engagement Project is the author and owner of these documents.
source.licence: Free to download, and no account needed.

preview.note: Worth a look even if you use something else entirely. Seeing three years mapped on one page is a good way to notice the gaps in your own plan.

preview.note: A good opener for a topical study, because it does the work of showing that the word carries more than one idea. Keep a note open while you watch and collect the passages it walks through — that list is most of your study already.

preview.note: A good opener for a topical study that would otherwise stall on unfamiliar ritual. Collect the passages it walks through and you have most of your outline.
